\section{Thermal model}
Let $C_1,C_2>0$ be constant heat capacities, let $G>0$ be a constant thermal conductance, and let $T_1(0),T_2(0)>0$. Time is denoted by $t$, and a dot denotes a time derivative. Each body has a single well-defined temperature. Heat capacity has units of energy per temperature, and conductance has units of energy per time per temperature. The contact has negligible heat capacity, and the pair exchanges no energy with its surroundings. The energy balances are
\begin{align}
 C_1\dot T_1&=-G(T_1-T_2),\label{eq:balance1}\\
 C_2\dot T_2&= G(T_1-T_2).\label{eq:balance2}
\end{align}
